newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL noon rubber up but buyers confused on ringgit.
newsitem.headline: KL noon rubber up but buyers confused on ringgit.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market was higher at midday as producers raised prices on renewed confidence but buyers were not committing due to uncertainties over the ringgit, traders said.
"The buyers are confused with the way the ringgit has been falling against the U.S. dollar...it's too fast for many to catch up," said a trader.
Traders said sentiment among producers or sellers was upbeat as the falling ringgit has made Malaysian rubber more competitive against Thai and Indonesian.
There were no confirmed reports of sales early Wednesday. But traders said some SMR grades could have been sold without the market's knowledge.

At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 buyer for August at 232.50 cents (91 U.S. cents) a kg, up 1.50 cents from Tuesday's close. The SMR20 buyer for August was also 1.50 cents up to 235.50.
Traders quoted the SMR 20 at 241 cents, SMR CV at 295, SMR L at 277, SMR5 at 248, SMR10 at 241 and drum latex at 193.
Malaysian-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
